steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (180 degrees C).
Place pork chops in a baking pan. Spread 1 teaspoon of butter over each chop, then spread 1 teaspoon of mayonnaise on top of butter.
Season each chop with seasoning salt, garlic powder, and parsley. Sprinkle 1/4 cup cheese over the top of each chop.
Bake in the preheated oven until pork is slightly pink in the center, about 35 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Simple Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: Learn how long to cook pork chops in the oven with this easy, cheesy baked pork chop recipe that makes a delicious dinner any day of the week.

video.description: Very easy pork chops to make! Just add a few spices, mayonnaise, butter, and cheese! Bake for just thirty-five minutes and serve alongside greens and potatoes!
video.name: Simple Time Pork Chops

review.reviewBody: I think this is the tastiest pork chop recipe I have ever had. I try to avoid butter and so instead I sprayed olive oil on the pork chops. They were delicious, thank you. My husband's favorite pork chop recipe now!

Wow! This was amazing - best pork chops ever! Super moist, lots of flavor and lots of compliments. I used Miracle Whip, didn't have mayo. I also didn't have seasoned salt, so I just used regular salt -- and, following the advice of others, I cut the amount of salt in half and it was plenty. I also mixed all of the ingredients, other than the cheese, and then spread it on the pork chops. The ONLY change I'll make next time is to stick the pan under the broiler when it's done cooking to brown the cheese. One very important note - I used a meat thermometer when I cooked the pork to make absolutely certain it was cooked to the temperature we like (150 degrees) -- once it hit 150, I pulled it out of the oven. I only had to cook it for 20 minutes, if I had cooked for the time recommended, I would have had shoe leather...

Delicious! Of course, I made a couple of changes:

• I combined the butter, mayonnaise, and seasonings together while the oven was heating and let the flavours blend into a compound butter/aioli. I also used minced garlic (1 tsp per chop) rather than garlic powder and added a little cayenne to perk up the taste.

• when the oven came up to temperature, I used a spatula to spread the butter mixture over the chops and then covered with cheese and baked as per directions.

• The pan juices were so flavourful that we couldn’t resist dipping our dinner rolls into the pan, but I think one could just as easily mix up extra butter/aioli and spread it on bread and sprinkle cheese to make incredible garlic bread using this recipe!

• The pan juices were so tasty that after dinner I mixed the remainder with a good amount of cream and made a wonderful savoury spread for the next morning’s bagels. Highly recommended!

Simple and easy. I put BBQ rub on my pork chops, seared on one side in a cast iron, flipped to the other side to sear and put in the oven. Added cheese on top the last 5 minutes. I never thought about putting cheese on top until now and it turned out wonderful!

I'd like to start by saying that I am not someone who generally likes pork and even I like this!

Dinner tonight started off with a different recipe so the pork was brined' the pork for 2 hours in a mix of water, salt, garlic, chili and lemongrass. I then patted it dry and put it on a tray before spreading margarine (my butter was rock solid) and the mayonnaise on top and adding the cheese. I let the cheese melt for about 15 minutes before adding some fresh parsley and letting it cook the rest of the way.

I was a bit sceptical about the mayonnaise and cheese with the pork but dinner turned out to be a big success and the guests thought it was 'something very different' and 'surprisingly delicious'! I will definitely be masking this again!

Like others, mixed butter and mayo the first time. (Other idea below) Thick chops so added mozzarella and cheddar cheeses later. Have made it a few times for the kids cuz it made it's way into the meal rotation plan.

An idea I borrowed from a steak recipe that works well. Can make a topping (minus cheese) ahead and store in the refrigerator for up to a few days ahead. Make a paste with softened butter, mayo and dry ingredients (plus parmesan , form the blend into an longed roll formed inside of a sheet of plastic wrap. Roll the plastic and store in the fridge till ready. Then cut evenly into pieces to put on top of pork.

This was delicious and easy to make. I mixed the butter and mayo together, but next time I'll omit the mayo, and I used garlic powder, onion powder, salt, pepper and dried parsley. It was super tasty, thank you!

Made it twice now. Family has declared it their new favorite meal. With how easy it is, and usually have all ingredients in the house, it is my new favorite to make! 
The second time I made it, I mixed together the mayo, butter and spices and then spread them on the pork chops. It was so much easier and didn't change the taste or presentation since the pretty spices are covered by cheese anyway. 
Love the "au juice" served over rice.

In my oven it took about 32 minutes. I highly recommend a digital meat thermometer, it makes all the difference in baking pork. I also used Cabot white cheddar. I didn't worry about slathering the butter perfectly or anything like that. I just put a chunk of butter spread out the mayonnaise and topped with cheese. What a nice recipe! This will be a go to for years after I get out of prison.

Oh my gosh my family loved these!!!! SO moist and tender. I cooked 6 boneless center cut chops according to the directions with a minor change. I used reduced fat ranch dressing instead of mayo because I don't like mayo and never have it on hand. I mixed the dressing and butter together and spread on top of the chops - much easier to spread the butter by doing that. I tried this recipe as a "tester" (tell my family if they don't like it, we'll go out to eat). It was unanimous - this recipe was added to the BOX! Such a great alternative to broiled or grilled pork chops that can sometimes be too dry.

Delicious but altered! I used a very small amount of butter and mayo. I didn't use the cheese because I am limiting the fat as much as possible right now. I also seasoned the chops with garlic salt on one side, Lawry's Season Salt on the other, and garlic powder. After seasoning the chops, I refrigerated them for two hours before baking. I will try them with the cheese at some point but honestly, they are fantastic even without the cheese!
Easy to make. Delicious, tender. Easy to change flavors by changing up the spices. Family loves it.

I have made these for years and just realized I never left a review. At first, I thought cheese on pork chops was a little differen, but my family loves them. Every time I cook them I have tasty and moist pork chops that get eaten up. The only thing I do different is I mix up the mayo & butter together and then spread the mixture on the chops. Great recipe!
It's delicious! Great flavor!! And moist!!
My boyfriend doesn't like pork chops too much says they always are dry not matter how you cook them but he loves these pork chops thank youu for the recipe I think they are great

To be fair I made the recipe as written minus the mayo because I didn't have any. Why are we adding salt when there is salt in the seasoned salt? Why are we adding garlic powder when there is garlic in the seasoned salt? 35 minutes is too long of a cook. We found these pork chops to be overcooked and tasted like a salt lick. I couldn't eat it and my family choked down what they could and threw the rest out. Anyone who said there was no flavor must have missed the seasoned salt. I'm sure I can figure out how to save this dish but this recipe as is does not work.

After reading other responses, I chose to add the spices first, then the butter, followed by the mayo and cheese per directions. It was ready in 30 minutes. My wife loved it, and now it's in our rotation.
I made this with no changes except omission of the cheese. It was fantastic Will make sure I have the cheese for the next time.

No flavour. The butter pooled at the bottom of the pan so that the chops were sitting in a puddle of grease. There was no flavour from the butter or the mayo. I even seasoned the chops with herbs and seasoning. I also felt pretty guilty about the calories and fat from the butter, mayo and cheese. Not really worth the calories and fat. Sorry, this one not for me. Thanks for the new dinner idea though.
This has to be the easiest and one of the most requested recipes I have... and it is always a smashing success with adults and kids, grandkids, and great-grandkids alike.
